questions.prompt: Explain the GIL. Given that, how do you write concurrent Python?
questions.zh: 解释一下 GIL。有了它，你会怎么写并发的 Python？
outline: The GIL lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time
Threads still work well for I/O-bound work, because the GIL is released while waiting
CPU-bound work goes to a process pool to use several cores
asyncio fits when there are many connections and little computation
A free-threaded build exists now, but most deployments still have the GIL

questions.prompt: Tell me about the pitfalls of async Python. What do you watch out for?
questions.zh: 讲讲异步 Python 的坑。你会注意什么？
outline: One blocking call inside a coroutine freezes the whole event loop
CPU work or blocking I/O must be handed to an executor
Cancellation is cooperative: tasks need cleanup in finally blocks
Timeouts and exception groups make failures visible instead of silent
How I test it: load the endpoint and watch for loop stalls

questions.prompt: What Python gotchas would you warn a junior developer about?
questions.zh: 有哪些 Python 的坑你会提醒初级开发者？
outline: A mutable default argument is shared between calls
Shallow copy versus deep copy when mutating nested data
Mutating a list while iterating over it skips elements
Naive versus aware datetimes cause subtle timezone bugs
Most of these bite silently, so tests matter more than memorization

questions.prompt: How do you keep a Python project maintainable once it is in production?
questions.zh: 一个 Python 项目上了生产之后，你怎么保持它可维护？
outline: Type hints on public functions, checked by a static type checker in CI
A virtual environment per project and pinned dependencies
dataclasses or TypedDict at the boundaries instead of loose dicts
pytest fixtures and parametrized tests keep the suite small
One linter-formatter, ruff, so style stops being a discussion

questions.prompt: A Python job is too slow. Walk me through how you would speed it up.
questions.zh: 一个 Python 任务太慢了。带我过一遍你会怎么优化。
outline: Profile the code first; the slow part is rarely where you guess
Fix the algorithm or the data structure before micro-optimizing
Cache repeated work with lru_cache where the inputs repeat
Generators keep memory flat on large inputs
Still CPU-bound: a process pool, or a C extension for the hot loop
